intro.title: useEffect & Side Effects
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple digital clock component that updates the displayed time every second. You will learn how to use the useEffect Hook to manage side effects—operations that interact with the outside world, like timers or data fetching. The main technologies involved are React for building the UI, TypeScript for type safety, and the useEffect Hook to handle the timer logic. By the end, you'll understand how to start and clean up side effects to keep your components efficient and bug-free.
intro.usecase: The useEffect hook is essential for managing side effects in real-world React applications, such as data fetching in dashboard components that update when filters change. You'll use it to synchronize component state with external systems like APIs, localStorage, or browser events in scenarios like live search inputs that debounce API calls. Common patterns include form validation that checks availability as users type, or analytics tracking that logs page views when route parameters change. This pattern appears in products like admin panels that fetch fresh data when users apply date filters, or e-commerce sites that update cart totals when items are modified.
